title: Q-BAG™
heroAlt: Provisional AI-generated artwork of a futuristic reusable Q-Bag travelling through a cosmic landscape
heroDeclaration: Buy the bag once. Refill it. Mark the journey. Bring it back.
heroSupport: A reusable coffee container and cultural refill protocol. Every return and personal mark adds history, making the object more uniquely yours—and increasingly difficult to throw away.

imageDisclosure.label: Temporary Visual Organism · AI-Generated
imageDisclosure.text: This image was made with generative AI under my direction while human creative time was temporarily scarce. It is not pretending to be handmade. One day it may be replaced, mutated, painted over, or respectfully composted.

introLead: Q-Bag is an artwork trying to manufacture a new social habit: buying coffee by weight in a reusable container, then allowing refill evidence and personal expression to accumulate on the object.
protocolLead: The refill action must remain almost boring. Personalisation is what makes the object singular; repetition is what gives that singular object a cultural life.

protocolSteps.detail: Begin with the official Q-Bag, then add your first personal sticker, drawing, name, or mark.
Bring the object to a participating roaster or refill-friendly coffee shop.
The café weighs the empty bag, adds coffee beans, and charges for the coffee.
A café stamp, refill mark, or occasional artist edition records that the performance happened.
Add your own stickers, drawings, repairs, and memories. The owner is a co-author, not only a customer.
The loop repeats. Wear, marks, places, and stories become part of the object.

ageingLead: Ordinary packaging loses value as it ages. Q-Bag is designed to do the opposite: every return gives its wear a reason to remain.

ageingStages.title: A new container
ageingStages.detail: Clean, useful, and still replaceable. The story has not started.

ageingStages.title: A recognisable habit
ageingStages.detail: The first refill marks and personal stickers appear. A favourite café and a visual identity begin to repeat.

ageingStages.title: A personal archive
ageingStages.detail: Chosen stickers, drawings, artists, dates, stains, and journeys make this bag unlike any other.

ageingStages.title: An object with gravity
ageingStages.detail: Throwing it away would mean discarding accumulated evidence of a life.

pilot.eyebrow: Proposed First Territory · Edinburgh or Elsewhere
pilot.title: One café. 100 Q-Bags. Three months.
pilot.body: The first pilot should be small enough to understand and strange enough to notice. Edinburgh is the home base, not the boundary: if the right café or person appears elsewhere in the world, Q-Bag is ready to travel.
measures: How often does each one return?
How many disposable bags are avoided?
Do owners photograph or share their changing bags?
pilot.metric: The magic metric is not bags sold. It is refills per Q-Bag.

operationalLayer.title: What happens behind the café counter?
operationalLayer.intro: Q-Bag should fit the equipment and rhythm a café already has. The first pilot tests a behaviour, not a new technology stack.

cafeFacts.label: Café does
cafeFacts.body: Tare the container, fill it with coffee beans, charge the customer, and add an optional refill mark.

cafeFacts.label: Café needs
cafeFacts.body: Existing scales, coffee beans, a clear reusable-container policy, and roughly ten seconds at the counter.

cafeFacts.label: Café gets
cafeFacts.body: Return visits, repeat bean sales, less packaging, participation in a visible artwork, and measured pilot results.

operationalLayer.pricingNote: The café chooses its own refill pricing. A discount is welcome, not required.
operationalLayer.backerIntro: A pilot backer helps the first 100 bags exist, travel, return, and produce evidence before anyone is asked to believe in global scale.
funds: Numbering, artwork, personalisation materials, and café instructions
Pilot documentation, measurement, and practical support
evidence: Participant photographs, stories, and a visual archive
Evidence for a better Q-Bag V2 and any future expansion
operationalLayer.closingNote: No platform. No app. No speculative machine required at the counter—only a useful object, an ordinary refill, and enough attention to learn what happens next.

prototypeRecord.label: Prototype Record / V0
prototypeRecord.title: It existed before it had a system.
prototypeRecord.body: Before Q-Bag became a formal refill protocol, I reused a resealable Artisan Roast retail coffee bag, personalised it with stickers and collage, and carried it during travel. It lasted for some time. The behaviour and attachment were already real; the measured pilot comes next.
prototypeRecord.boundary: FIELD NOTE: These photographs document a personal prototype. They do not establish food-safety approval, freshness performance, or café workflow; those questions belong to V1.

participantCards.title: For coffee drinkers
participantCards.body: Better coffee, less packaging, and an ordinary object that becomes unmistakably yours.

participantCards.title: For cafés and roasters
participantCards.body: A visible refill culture, repeat visits, collaborative editions, and less single-use packaging.

participantCards.title: For artists
participantCards.body: A recurring canvas that travels through cafés and kitchens instead of waiting in storage.

valueCircuit.title: A useful loop can fund what comes next.
valueCircuit.intro: Q-Bag is openly commercial, but its first economy is practical: a person returns, a café sells more coffee, packaging is avoided, the object gains identity, and Q888 earns resources and experience to improve the experiment.

stages.label: Return for coffee
stages.body: The owner brings back a useful object instead of replacing another anonymous package.

stages.label: Café earns a repeat visit
stages.body: The café sells beans, strengthens a customer relationship, and participates in a visible refill culture.

stages.label: The bag gains identity
stages.body: Marks, wear, places, and personal choices make reuse emotionally easier and the object harder to discard.

stages.label: Revenue funds the next layer
stages.body: Income and evidence can support better containers, new café pilots, artists, travel, and future Q888 work.

valueCircuit.collectorBonus: Creative meaning and financial survival are not enemies. The artwork creates desire and attachment; the operating loop creates evidence and income; each can help the other remain alive.
valueCircuit.clarityNote: This is intended commercial activity: useful objects and pilot participation may create revenue. The deeper possibility of collectability belongs to the speculative layer below, where it remains possible rather than promised.

speculativeBoundary.title: The ambition is real. The return is not promised.
speculativeBoundary.body: Infocigan is transparent artistic commerce. Q-Bag wants to earn money, accumulate experience, create opportunities for collaborators, and reinvest those resources into future Q888 work. Its exaggerated market language laughs at financial theatre without pretending that artists can live without money.
speculativeBoundary.disclaimer: BUY THE OBJECT FOR ITS USE, ART, RITUAL, AND MEANING. IF FUTURE COLLECTORS DECIDE IT IS WORTH MORE, THAT IS YOUR PERSONAL BONUS FOR TRUST—NOT A GUARANTEE FROM Q888.

conceptCards.title: Q-Bag is the protocol
paragraphs: Q-Bag is not another disposable-packaging brand. It is a shared refill behaviour with a recognisable object at its centre. The official bag is the protocol's native vessel and visible flag; future guest vessels may participate when they are safe and suitable.
The bag can travel between cafés, roasteries, kitchens, cities, and artist editions. The system becomes more valuable when the behaviour spreads—not when more unused bags are manufactured.

conceptCards.title: Marks as evidence and identity
paragraphs: Q-Bag carries two kinds of marks. Protocol marks prove that refills happened: a small stamp, a date, or an occasional edition made with a café, artist, festival, or cultural project.

Personal marks belong entirely to the owner. Their own stickers, drawings, writing, repairs, and visual decisions turn the standard Q-Bag into a unique object and create the attachment that makes long-term reuse emotionally natural.
Not every refill needs new material, but every owner needs room to become the bag's co-author. A Q-Bag is never finished; it becomes specific through use and personalisation.

conceptCards.title: Reuse becomes identity
paragraphs: Sustainability here is not framed as punishment or purity. It becomes a visible habit: one durable object repeatedly returning for coffee instead of being replaced by another anonymous package.
The aim is not to preach. It is to make reuse more socially legible, more personal, and eventually more desirable than waste.

conceptCards.title: Trust may acquire value
paragraphs: Cultural or resale value is not guaranteed, but may emerge through participation. An early café edition might become meaningful, a bag might become recognisable within a city, or a completely personal design might someday find another collector willing to pay for its history.
All outcomes are valid. The experiment is the point.

partnersParagraphs: Q-Bag is designed to meet coffee businesses where refill behaviour already exists: a tare-and-fill routine, a clear reusable-container policy, light-touch marks, and occasional collaborative editions. Revenue and experience from the system can be reinvested into pilots, artists, travel, and future Q888 projects.

The immediate invitation is not to scale a bag company. It is to find the right first café—in Edinburgh or anywhere in the world—willing to host and measure the first 100-bag experiment. Edinburgh is where I am; the protocol is willing to travel.
closingLines: Every reuse is a small act of resistance.
